summary.title: Meetings for an effective eng organization
summary.one_liner: Learn which six core meetings (plus a few optional ones) Will Larson recommends for an engineering organization, and how to run, scale, and assign owners for them.
keywords: how to run effective meetings engineering
takeaways: Six core meetings to start with: weekly team meeting, technical spec review, incident review, engineering managers monthly, staff engineers monthly, and a monthly engineering Q&A.
Meetings are a backup communication channel; written documents and tickets are the preferred primary approach.
Review meetings work best when attendees read a written document first and the author does not simply present it.
Scale operational meetings by participant relevance and developmental meetings by engagement (e.g. split when more than about ten people attend).
Attend meetings regularly and hold disruptive participants accountable, since leaders' behavior sets the norm and splitting meetings is often premature.
summary.summary: Will Larson argues that well-run engineering meetings act as the heartbeat of an organization, even though many meetings are poor. He recommends six core meetings grouped into operational (weekly leadership/team meeting, technical spec review, incident review), developmental (engineering managers and staff engineers monthlies), and a monthly engineering Q&A. The chapter gives concrete facilitation tips such as running a shared agenda, requiring pre-reading, using anonymous question tools, and assigning dedicated owners. It also covers optional meetings like execution reviews, demos, and all-hands, plus guidance on scaling meetings, 1:1s, and skip-levels. The text is an unedited excerpt from O'Reilly's The Engineering Executive's Primer.
